findings.summary: The plan never says what main's check does in the gap between a merge and the landing record written after it, or where 'nothing unverified reaches main' is now enforced.
findings.evidence: Decision 2 says main's check requires every first-parent commit to be named by a landing or intervention record. Decision 5 writes that record only after the host merges. A check that runs on the push to main will therefore find the new tip unattributed on every landing. That is the same kind of red main the request is trying to end. Once trailers are gone, the gate that stops unverified content reaching main has to move to a pre-merge check on the pull request's head, and the plan does not name it. Fix: Add a decision on the ordering. Example: a required pre-merge status on the PR verifies the head and the prediction, and that is where 'nothing unverified reaches main' is enforced. After the merge, the attribution check runs when the records branch is pushed, or it treats the tip as 'pending reconciliation' for a bounded time before failing. Put both locations in the guarantees table.

findings.summary: The demonstration commands would not show the content they claim to observe.
findings.evidence: Criterion 1 runs `git diff --stat`, which lists file names, not the options comparison. Criteria 2–7 run `git show HEAD:docs/design/records-history.md`, but the producer does not commit (Athena owns commits), so in the working tree that file does not exist at HEAD and the command errors. Fix: Read the working-tree file instead, e.g. `grep -n` for the section headings and the exempt commit ids in docs/design/records-history.md. Use `git status --porcelain` together with `git diff --stat` for criterion 9 so the new untracked file is listed.

findings.summary: The reachability mechanism is left as an either/or, and one option would not keep the commits.
findings.evidence: The plan offers 'refs/athena/pr/<n> (or storing a bundle/tree-and-commit objects in the records branch as a gitlink-free tag/ref)'. Commit objects stored as tree entries or gitlinks are not reachable for git's garbage collection. Refs pushed to the host still live on the host. Fix: Choose one mechanism, e.g. keep-refs under refs/athena/pr/* that are mirrored with the records ref on lift-out, or a records-branch commit that takes the PR head as a parent. State how it survives garbage collection and a mirror clone, and how it works in D72 stealth mode.

findings.summary: Reconciliation asks the host which PR was merged, which sits awkwardly with the aim of not depending on the host.
findings.evidence: 'looks up the merged PR via the host'. The landing-intent record already holds the PR head, so a squash whose tree equals that head could be matched locally. Fix: Match main commits against landing-intent records first (tree equals the recorded head), and use the host only as a fallback.

summary: The plan answers the request and the accepted reading: three files, D112 appended after D111 with status Proposed, a recommendation of a separate-root records branch weighed against A4, A5 and D72, and all seven points in the document. I checked the repository: D111 is the last entry in docs/decisions.md; earlier entries use 'Decision: Proposed'; athena.toml's [history] exempt list holds the six commit ids the plan names; and BRIEF.md lines 1038–1039 carry Sri's words as quoted. One major gap remains. Once landing records are written after the merge, the plan does not say how main's check avoids going red between the merge and the record write, or where 'nothing unverified reaches main' is enforced instead. That is central to criterion 4 and to the request's aim of ending a red main. The minor findings: most demonstration commands would not show the content they claim (`git show HEAD:` on an uncommitted file, `git diff --stat` for a content check), and the PR-commit reachability mechanism is left undecided. Revise.
